decisions.executionNote: Approach the red nut with the left arm, gradually pitching downward and retaining elbow-up continuity; right arm stays parked.
Finish a vertical approach above the red nut using head projection and wrist feedback; remain open pending alignment.
Lower to the red nut grasp height with a small lateral correction; inspect centering before closing.
Center the red nut, close fully, then lift vertically to check retention in RGB.
Red nut is visibly retained. Carry it above the matching red bolt with clearance, then inspect axial alignment.
Lower the retained red nut toward the bolt, using the wrist image for a small lateral correction and keeping the axis vertical.
Begin clockwise threading of the red nut with a gentle axial descent; watch for retained alignment rather than assuming engagement.
Release and reset the left wrist without reversing the nut, then regrasp for another clockwise tightening sweep.
Continue clockwise red-nut tightening while following the thread downward slightly; hold closed through the sweep.
Reset the open left wrist for another red tightening sweep. Bring the right arm to a high preparation pose in its own workspace.
Third clockwise sweep on red with slight downward following. Finish orienting the right gripper downward at a clear waiting pose.
Open and reset the left wrist, leaving the red nut on its matching bolt, then close for the next tightening sweep.
Apply a further clockwise red-nut sweep, keeping the grip closed and following the thread by a small axial amount.
Release, unwind only the open gripper, and regrasp the red nut for continued tightening.
Continue the red nut clockwise after the regrasp, with a small axial following motion.
Reset the open wrist without unthreading the red nut, then close for a final tightening pass.
Allow the red regrasp to settle, then perform the last clockwise sweep with slight axial following.
Release the tightened red pair, lift clear, and move the open left gripper above the purple nut. Keep right arm waiting clear of the handoff region.
Replan from the interrupted pose using smaller combined translation and yaw increments to approach the purple nut.
Descend open over the purple nut, correcting the small head-projected offset and restoring a vertical grasp axis.
Correct the rejected tensor without compensating for unexecuted motion: center on purple, close, and lift to inspect retention.
Purple nut is visible between the fingers. Carry it to the central placement area for a table-mediated handoff, keeping right arm clear.
Place the purple nut upright on the central table area and open the left gripper before retreating for the right-arm pickup.
Lift the open left gripper and retreat left; only then bring the right gripper toward the centrally placed purple nut, without crossing arms.
Bring the right gripper down above the central purple nut, with the left arm stationary and clear; inspect before closing.
Lower to the central purple nut, close the right gripper, and lift vertically to check that the table handoff was retained.
Carry the visibly retained purple nut above its right-side bolt. Once the center is clear, move the open left arm toward the gray nut at a safe height.
Align and lower the purple nut toward its bolt using wrist feedback. Independently bring the open left gripper above the gray nut, keeping arm separation.
Make a small purple axis correction and start a gentle clockwise engagement. Lower the open left gripper toward gray, stopping short for visual alignment.
Continue gently seating and turning purple clockwise, while bringing the left gripper to the gray nut grasp height.
Grasp and lift the gray nut with the left arm. Open and reset the right wrist over purple to inspect its seating before another tightening grasp.
Purple appears seated with the bolt filling its bore; leave it released and lift clear. Carry the retained gray nut to the central table handoff area.
Set the gray nut upright at the central handoff spot and release. Keep the right arm clear while correcting its small tilt.
Lift and retreat the open left arm from gray. Approach the handoff area with the right arm only after the left has moved clear.
Approach the centrally placed gray nut with the right gripper open. Begin retracting the empty left arm toward origin through its existing elbow-up branch.
Fine-center and grasp the gray nut with the right arm, then lift to verify retention. Finish returning the open left arm toward its origin.
Carry the retained gray nut above its matching right-side bolt with clearance. Settle the empty left arm at origin.
Lower the retained gray nut toward its bolt with a small lateral correction from the wrist image; keep the bore vertical.
Correct gray alignment slightly left, then begin clockwise engagement with a gentle downward following motion; keep the left arm parked.
Release gray and reset only the open wrist. The bore looks offset and tracking showed contact, so inspect seating before applying another turn.
Gray has fallen beside rather than onto its bolt. Reposition the open right gripper over the displaced nut for a fresh, centered grasp.
Fine-center on the displaced gray nut, close fully and lift clear for a fresh alignment attempt; verify retention visually.
The gray nut was not retained. Reopen and descend more carefully to a slightly lower grasp height, then inspect centering before closing again.
Gray is centered at grasp height. Close and pause, then lift straight up while removing the small contact-induced tilt; verify retention from the next image.
Gray is visibly retained now. Move above the bolt with clearance, using the head-projected bolt axis rather than the previous offset placement.
Lower gray slowly toward the bolt, making a millimeter-scale axis correction from the wrist view; postpone turning until seating is visible.
The gray bore still shows a small offset. Nudge toward the bolt along the table while applying a slow clockwise seating turn with minimal descent.
Continue a slow gray seating turn with a controlled axial descent, staying within wrist range and checking whether the bolt enters the bore.
Contact is obstructing gray rather than cleanly threading. Lift to relieve the obstruction, then restore wrist range while checking whether the nut remains held.
Straighten the held gray nut at a clear height and recenter above the bolt before another descent; the prior contact had introduced tilt.
Compensate for the gray nut's visible fore-aft shift within the grip while descending slowly; keep its axis vertical and inspect before turning.
Make a slow fore-aft centering correction for the shifted gray grasp with almost no descent; inspect bore alignment before applying torque.
The gray bolt is now visible in the bore. Turn clockwise about the estimated nut axis, compensating for its offset within the grip rather than rotating about link6 alone.
Follow the gray nut downward with a small further clockwise turn, compensating its in-grip offset and staying short of the wrist limit.
Release gray without further lateral force and lift clear to inspect its actual seating. Reset the empty wrist only after clearance.
Gray remains beside its bolt. Approach the released nut for a centered, upright regrasp and restore the standard downward wrist orientation.
Use wrist centering to descend toward gray with reduced pregrasp opening, avoiding the adjacent bolt; pause at grasp height before closing.
Finish centering gray at grasp height, close and settle before lifting vertically to verify a stable, centered regrasp.
With gray now centered in the fingers, lift slightly and translate over the bolt axis for a fresh vertical insertion, avoiding lateral contact.
Descend straight over the gray bolt with the centered grasp, without twisting or lateral movement, to check seating at the insertion height.
The gray bolt now occupies the bore. Apply a slow clockwise tightening sweep with minimal axial following, checking for tilt or lateral displacement.
Lift gray out of the obstructed insertion and move to clear right-side space while retaining it. The turning contact indicates a remaining in-grip offset requiring a centered regrasp.
Move gray to an unobstructed right-side table spot and restore a vertical wrist for a deliberate centered regrasp away from the bolt.
Set gray down in the clear area, release it to settle upright, and lift the open fingers for a fresh visual alignment.
Regrasp the settled gray nut in clear space, correcting its fore-aft center before closing at the standard grasp height.
Refine the gray grasp fore-aft from the wrist image, then close and lift clear with the nut centered on the turning axis.
Carry the newly centered gray nut above its matching bolt at clearance height, retaining a vertical turning axis.
Lower the centered gray nut straight to the bolt with only a small lateral alignment correction; inspect seating before turning.
Gray appears centered over the bolt. Apply a short, slow clockwise sweep with negligible axial descent and inspect for any lateral shift.
Pause turning and make a slow fore-aft correction toward the bolt axis visible in the rotated wrist view, without adding downward pressure.
Use the rotated wrist view to bring the bolt cap toward the bore center with a small planar correction, keeping height and rotation fixed.
The bolt now fills the visible gray bore. Apply a slow clockwise seating sweep with slight descent and a small compensation for the estimated in-grip offset.
Pause rotation near the wrist limit and lower gray slowly, making a small correction toward the cap visible in the bore; monitor for obstruction.
The gray cap now fills the bore. Release and reset only the open wrist in place, then regrasp for another clockwise tightening sweep.
Gray remains visibly seated after release. Center the open fingers on its shifted bore before closing fully, to avoid turning about an offset axis.
With the gray bore centered and its cap visible, apply a slow clockwise tightening sweep while following the thread down slightly.
Release and reset only the open right wrist, then regrasp the seated gray nut for another clockwise tightening sweep.
